issue.description: BR-T18 remediation found that the closed ruleset does not produce a fingerprint for an AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY assignment stored in semantic bead text, although the repository gitleaks policy identifies it. Add a near-zero-false-positive provider rule anchored to the exact AWS environment-variable name and 40-character secret shape, bump the compiled ruleset version, retain placeholder downgrading and non-disclosing output, and add prevention plus historical-redaction conformance. No credential bytes belong in fixtures, logs, commands, or output.
issue.notes:

issue.description:
ADR-003 records that `cmd_sync_flush_only` hardcodes `CheckpointMode::Monolithic`, making the sharded, content-addressed checkpoint writer required by section 6.1.1 unreachable dead code — one of the three documented defects behind unbounded checkpoint growth under per-mutation flushing. The other two defects have open beads (content-address the monolithic root: beadrs-8daa18dc; apply pointer-declared tombstones: beadrs-a5f95091); this one has none. Either expose sharded mode (e.g. a checkpoint.mode config/flag, with equivalence and migration tests across modes) or delete the unreachable writer and update section 6.1.1 / ADR-003 so the documented checkpoint design and the code agree.

---
Priority: P2
Created by: weave strand
issue.title: Make sharded checkpoint mode reachable or remove the dead writer (ADR-003 defect 1)
